To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the production model of corporate governance recommends that the corporate board be a deliberative body that is composed of a select group of independent, outside and insider directors who represent the firm's stakeholders, and whose audit, compensation, and nomination committees are comprised solely of independent outside directors.

the production model of corporate governance suggests that the board should be a forum for deliberation, not a body for oversight, that the board should represent the interests of all stakeholders, not just those of investors and that the board should include insiders, not just outsiders.
the production model of corporate governance calls for a board of directors that is more inclusive, more deliberative and more independent.
